name: Museo Nacional de Artes Visuales
funding: Uruguayan state museum, a division of the Dirección Nacional de Cultura in the Ministry of Education and Culture.
watch: Created by Law 3,932 of 10 December 1911 as the Museo de Bellas Artes. Roxana Fabius has directed it since August 2025.
records_note: The museum has nothing of its own; its ministry posts annual memorias for 2010 to 2023, but no museum accounts, funder list or board.

name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes de La Habana
funding: State museum subordinate to Cuba's Ministry of Culture.
watch: The October 2021 boycott letter targets the Havana Biennial and the government, not this museum.
records_note: Its official site could not be reached from here, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked.

name: Museum Ludwig
funding: A museum of the City of Cologne, founded 1976 with the Peter and Irene Ludwig donation. The Ludwig Foundation, the Friends and the Gesellschaft für Moderne Kunst support it.
watch: Municipal museum run by the City of Cologne's cultural administration.
records_note: A Cologne city museum with no report or board of its own; the city posts accounts 2008 to 2023; it names 41 partners, undated.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Skopje
funding: Skopje's Town Assembly founded it in 1964 from donated art; Poland gave the building design. The Ministry of Culture and Tourism approves its annual programme projects.
watch: Holds over 5,500 works. Director Mira Gaćina, in post since 2017, resigned for personal reasons after six years; Tihomir Topuzovski is acting director.
records_note: Its site posts the ministry-approved 2025 programme but no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; only staff are named.

name: Nasher Museum of Art at Duke
funding: Part of Duke University. Founding gift from Raymond Nasher; a national Board of Advisors and a Friends Board guide fundraising; Annual Fund, endowment and exhibition gifts.
watch: The pin's tobacco-origin note is a historical link only. No current tobacco funder, objection or controversy at the museum turned up.
records_note: A Duke unit: annual reports 2006 to 2022 on its site, Duke posts audited statements, the Board of Advisors is listed, donor lists are old.

name: National Art Museum of China
funding: State museum funded by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism. About 1.05 million visitors in 2016. German collectors Peter and Irene Ludwig donated 117 works.
watch: Opened in 1963; holds over 110,000 works. Jean Nouvel's larger building was announced in 2014; no budget for either was found.
records_note: Its own site is unreachable; an archived copy shows no reports, funders or board, and its ministry publishes final accounts covering it.

name: National Art Museum of Moldova
funding: State museum subordinate to Moldova's Ministry of Culture.
watch: Holds 39,767 works and had 81,147 visitors in 2024. Its Dadiani wing restoration began in 2004; the second sector opened in September 2021.
records_note: Posts one activity report, for 2024, and yearly management declarations; no audited accounts, funder list or named board members.

name: National Arts Festival
funding: Eastern Cape government, Sarah Baartman District Municipality, National Lottery Commission, Standard Bank. National government gave R5.5 million for 2022 to 2024, nothing in 2025, a smaller grant in 2026.
watch: Minister McKenzie says it lost an open call. A January 2026 petition of 302 artists cites the cut among his refusals to renew funding.
records_note: Names its eleven-member board and management, and two presenting sponsors in text with logos for the rest; no annual reports or accounts found.

name: National Gallery of Arts Tirana
funding: Albanian state museum under the Ministry of Economy, Culture and Innovation, per Wikipedia.
watch: Holds over 5,000 works. Closed for rebuilding with a new annex since 2021, per Wikipedia; in October 2024 the ministry gave no deadline.
records_note: Its official site does not load, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; its ministry publishes no gallery-level accounts that were found.

name: National Museum of Contemporary Art (MNAC)
funding: Romanian Ministry of Culture funds it, including RON 500,000 for 2024 acquisitions. Sponsors include AQUA Carpatica, Greentek Lighting, Crama Oprișor, Molotow, UniCredit Bank and BRD Groupe Société Générale.
watch: Opened 2004 inside the Palace of the Parliament. ArtMargins writer Augustin Ioan said in 2008 that Prime Minister Nastase financed it in secret.
records_note: Its Partners and Sponsors page shows logos only; no annual reports, accounts or board list are posted, only ministry orders on its regulations.

name: National Museum of Fine Arts of Chile (MNBA)
funding: State museum under the Servicio Nacional del Patrimonio Cultural; buys works from its own budget. Gifts came through Fundación AMA from collector Juan Yarur Torres and from artist Cecilia Vicuña.
watch: 510,720 visitors in 2024, a decade high. Cancelled a León Ferrari retrospective in June 2026, citing budget cuts. Not the Buenos Aires museum.
records_note: MNBA has no records of its own; its parent service posts accountability reports 2006 to 2026 and financial statements 2017 to 2025.

name: Nesr Art Foundation
funding: Funded by Wissam and Hiba Nesr. Wissam is chief executive of Webcor Group, a Swiss-based food importer and distributor with most African revenue in Angola. No outside funders named.
watch: Opened in 2021 with a residency for Angolan and Lusophone African artists; the artistic committee is chaired by Paula Nascimento.
records_note: Names its eight-member advisory board and three-member artistic committee; publishes no annual reports, accounts or funder list, being paid for by its founders.
